title: The system: a photo-sharing app, every box labelled with its number
caption: Read the sub-labels: 23 writes/s, 17k reads/s, 5.5 PB and 23 Gbps each pick a different component.

steps.text: Five assumptions drive everything: 10 M daily users, 1 in 5 posts a photo a day, each views 50, 500 KB per photo, peak = 3× average.
Writes: 2 M uploads/day ÷ 1e5 s ≈ 23/s. That is tiny: one Upload API pool and one database primary, no sharding.
Bytes: 2 M × 500 KB = 1 TB/day, ×3 replicas, ×5 years ≈ 5.5 PB. That number alone says object storage, never database rows. Resizing goes through a queue so uploads return fast.
Metadata is a different number: 1 KB per photo ≈ 2 GB/day, about 3.6 TB in 5 years. One relational primary holds it.
Reads: 500 M views/day ≈ 5 800/s, 17 400/s at peak, past one database. A cache with ~95% hits leaves under 1 000 reads/s for the DB and its replicas.
Egress: 5 800 × 500 KB × 8 ≈ 23 Gbps on average, ~70 Gbps at peak. Only a CDN serves that; the photo store sees misses only.

scenarios.name: 8 pm peak
scenarios.summary: Design for the peak, not the average: 3× the reads and egress arrive at once, and only the read path and the edge feel it.

steps.text: Evening peak: 17 400 views/s and ~70 Gbps of photo bytes.
The CDN serves ~66 Gbps from the edge; the origin sends ~3.5 Gbps.
The Photo API pool scales out to ~4 servers; the cache takes ~16 500 reads/s.
Uploads peak at ~70/s: still nothing for the write path.

scenarios.name: Cache down
scenarios.summary: Lose the cache and 17 400 reads/s land on a tier sized for 900: the estimate tells you the replicas or a warm standby cache must exist.

steps.text: The metadata cache cluster restarts empty during peak.
All 17 400 reads/s go to a database tier sized for ~900 misses/s: about 20× its normal load.
Mitigate: shed non-critical reads, warm the cache from recent photos, and keep a replica cache in another zone.

scenarios.name: Viral photo
scenarios.summary: One photo, 1 M views in an hour (~280/s): per-key load is small, and the CDN and cache serve it. The total, not one key, drives the design here.

steps.text: A photo goes viral: 1 M views in an hour ≈ 280/s, ~1 Gbps for that one object.
The first request per edge misses and fetches from the store; then the edge serves it.
Its metadata is one hot cache key at 280 reads/s: fine for one cache node.
